## Load packages

```{r}
library(edgeR)
library(filbinverse)
library(ggplot2)
library(glue)
library(Matrix)
library(qs)
library(Seurat)
```

## Preparing environment

```{r}
base_dir <- '/n/data1/dfci/pedonc/filbin/lab/users/cao385/Projects/Synaptic'

## Loading custom functions
source(glue('{base_dir}/Synaptic2024/scripts/resources/utils.R'))

sample_col <- "sample"
assay_use  <- "RNA"
slot_use   <- "counts"
min_cells_per_sample <- 20
```

## Loading Seurat object

```{r}
data <- qread(glue('{base_dir}/output/Integrated_noBatch.qs'))
```

## Filtering samples with few cells and pseudobulking

```{r}
DefaultAssay(data) <- assay_use

counts <- GetAssayData(data, assay = assay_use, slot = slot_use)

# Keep samples with enough cells
tab <- table(data@meta.data[[sample_col]])
keep_samples <- names(tab)[tab >= min_cells_per_sample]

cells_keep <- rownames(data@meta.data)[data@meta.data[[sample_col]] %in% keep_samples]
data2 <- subset(data, cells = cells_keep)

counts2 <- GetAssayData(data2, assay = assay_use, slot = slot_use)
sample_ids <- data2@meta.data[[sample_col]]

# Sparse model matrix: cells -> sample membership
mm <- sparse.model.matrix(~ 0 + sample_ids)
colnames(mm) <- sub("^sample_ids", "", colnames(mm))

# Pseudobulk: genes x samples (sum of counts)
pb_counts <- counts2 %*% mm

# Optional: clean column names
colnames(pb_counts) <- make.names(colnames(pb_counts))
```

## Normalizing data

```{r}
dge <- DGEList(counts = pb_counts)
dge <- calcNormFactors(dge, method = "TMM")

# log2-CPM with prior count for stability
pb_logcpm <- cpm(dge, log = TRUE, prior.count = 1)
```

## Filter and selection of genes

```{r}
gene_names <- rownames(pb_logcpm)

ribosomal <- grepl("^RPS|^RPL", gene_names)

# optional extras
mito <- grepl("^MT-", gene_names)
hb   <- grepl("^HB[AB]", gene_names)

exclude <- ribosomal | mito | hb

pb_logcpm_filt <- pb_logcpm[!exclude, ]

n_hvg <- 2000

# Choose variable genes across samples
vars <- apply(pb_logcpm_filt, 1, var)
hvg <- names(sort(vars, decreasing = TRUE))[seq_len(min(n_hvg, length(vars)))]
```

## Calculate PCA

```{r}
# PCA expects samples as rows
pca <- prcomp(t(pb_logcpm[hvg, ]), center = TRUE, scale. = TRUE)

var_exp <- (pca$sdev^2) / sum(pca$sdev^2) * 100
pc1_pct <- round(var_exp[1], 1)
pc2_pct <- round(var_exp[2], 1)

# Data frame for plotting
pca_df <- data.frame(
  sample = rownames(pca$x),
  PC1 = pca$x[, 1],
  PC2 = pca$x[, 2],
  PC3 = pca$x[, 3],
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)
```

## Plot by tumor_type

```{r}
tumor_col <- "tumor_type"  # <-- change this to your tumor type column

# Build one-row-per-sample metadata table
meta <- data2@meta.data[, c(sample_col, tumor_col), drop = FALSE]

# If tumor type is constant per sample, take the most frequent value
meta_sample <- aggregate(
  meta[[tumor_col]],
  by = list(sample = meta[[sample_col]]),
  FUN = function(x) names(sort(table(x), decreasing = TRUE))[1]
)
colnames(meta_sample)[2] <- tumor_col
meta_sample$sample <- make.names(meta_sample$sample)

# Join to PCA df
pca_df_2 <- merge(pca_df, meta_sample, by = "sample", all.x = TRUE)

pca_df_2$tumor_type <- factor(pca_df_2$tumor_type, levels = names(colors_dataset_all))

pt <- ggplot(pca_df_2, aes(x = PC1, y = PC2, color = .data[[tumor_col]])) +
  geom_point(size = 3) +
  scale_color_manual(values = colors_dataset_all) +
  seurat_theme() +
  labs(
    x = paste0("PC1 (", pc1_pct, "%)"),
    y = paste0("PC2 (", pc2_pct, "%)"),
    color = 'Dataset'
  )

ggsave(plot = pt, filename = glue('{base_dir}/output/PCA_Samples-tumor_type.pdf'), width = 8, height = 5)
```
